title: Resilience-by-Contract: API Manifest and Validation Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines a lightweight, machine-readable API manifest and an associated validation pipeline that ensures every public-facing service at Redwood carries a minimal resilience and observability contract. The goal is to catch contract regressions early (CI), verify runtime assumptions (staging/canary), and continuously validate observability signals in production without heavy operational overhead.

Why this exists:
- Production inference requires predictable behavior across high-throughput, low-latency paths; API surface regressions are a leading source of incidents.
- A standardized manifest lets automation verify contracts across CI, canaries, and runtime monitors.
- Manifest-driven validation reduces ad-hoc test coverage and creates a consistent signal taxonomy for SRE and product teams.

Scope:
- Applies to all public REST/gRPC endpoints that serve customer requests (hosted API, Dedicated control plane endpoints, and Private control-plane adapters).
- Excludes purely internal tooling endpoints used only by ops if they are behind internal ACLs and have separate runbooks.

Manifest format (recommended minimal fields):
- Each service should check in a manifest file at the repo root: api-manifest.json or api-manifest.yaml
- Manifests are small (under 2KB) and intended to be validated by CI and the runtime intake system.

Sample manifest (JSON):
{
  "api_name": "synthesis-service",
  "contract_id": "synth-v3",
  "schema_checksum": "sha256:3a7b...e9f",
  "routes": [
    {
      "path": "/v1/generate",
      "method": "POST",
      "required_headers": ["Authorization", "X-Request-ID"],
      "sample_payload_location": "tests/fixtures/generate-basic.json"
    }
  ],
  "slo": {
    "p50_ms": "40",
    "p95_ms": "120",
    "p99_ms": "350",
    "error_rate_pct": "0.5"
  },
  "observability": {
    "required_metrics": ["request_latency_ms", "backend_error_count", "queue_depth"],
    "trace_sample_rate": "0.02"
  },
  "canary_checks": ["schema-compat", "latency-regression", "functional-end-to-end"],
  "owner": "team-synthesis"
}

Validation pipeline (high level):
1) Pre-merge CI checks (fast, must pass before merge):
   - Manifest lint: schema present, fields typed, checksum format validated.
   - Schema contract test: basic shape checks against canonical schema.
   - Smoke functional test: run sample payload against local stub or staging cluster (timeout 2s).
   - Artifact signing present for model-backed endpoints (if model_id referenced).
2) Staging/canary validation (post-merge):
   - Canary traffic (0.5% initial): verify P95 and error rate within manifest SLO.
   - Observability assertions: required metrics emitted, trace spans contain required attributes (request_id, model_version).
   - Schema drift detector: compare production response shape to schema_checksum; fail on unknown top-level keys unless flagged as opt-in.
3) Production continuous validation (rolling monitors):
   - Telemetry heartbeat: metric emission every minute per 1000 requests; missing heartbeat for 10m triggers operational alert.
   - Drift windows: weekly sample-based schema-diff; if drift > 2% of responses, open an automated issue and notify owner.

Validation stages table (text):
| Stage | Trigger | Max latency to detect | Action on failure | Owner |
| CI | PR opened | immediate | Block merge | Dev |
| Canary | New deployment | 30m | Automated rollback and notify | SRE + Dev |
| Production monitor | continuous | 10m | Pager/automated mitigation, open ticket | SRE |

CI gating rules (detailed):
- All PRs that modify code paths touching a route listed in api-manifest.json must:
  1. Bump manifest "schema_checksum" when schema changes.
  2. Add/adjust sample_payloads for regression tests.
  3. Provide at least one targeted unit test that validates error and success paths for the new behavior.
- The CI system will run schema-compatibility checks using the manifest checksum and the canonical schema stored in /infra/schemas. Failing compatibility prevents merge.

Runtime checks and telemetry (implementation guidance):
- Required metrics (from manifest) must be emitted with the following tags/dimensions: service, route, tenant_id (if multi-tenant), host_region, model_variant (if applicable).
- Traces must add the attribute redwood.contract_id with the manifest contract_id. This lets the observability pipeline join contract validation events with traces.
- Error classification: any 5xx is a candidate for contract violation if accompanied by a missing required field in response payload.
- Sampling: default trace_sample_rate is 0.02; teams may increase for canaries to 1.0 for a 30-minute window.

Failure modes and remediation playbook (quick reference):
1) CI manifest lint failure: fix schema or update manifest; include a short changelog entry in the PR.
2) Canary latency regression: automatic rollback to previous stable artifact if P95 exceeds manifest.p95_ms by >40% for 10 minutes.
3) Schema drift detection (production): create ticket with sample diffs, set temporary sampling to 100% for 30 minutes, and notify the owner.
4) Missing telemetry heartbeat: run the ops checklist: check exporter health, inspect sidecar logs, check feature flags, use curl against /health.

Rollout and ownership:
- Ownership model: owner in manifest should reference a single team alias (team-foo). That team is responsible for creating an incident runbook entry and ensuring a 1-hour on-call response for manifest-based regressions.
- Rollout cadence: new manifests introduced without migrations must be gated behind a canary of at least 1 hour at 1% traffic and 2 hours at 5% before full rollout.
- Escalation: SRE owns the rollback decision for canary-stage violations; development team owns root-cause and follow-up.

Automation roadmap (recommended automation to build):
- Linter plugin for repo check (pre-commit) that enforces presence of manifest and sanity checks.
- CI job that validates sample payloads against a running staging instance using the manifest.
- Observability pipeline enrichment that attaches contract_id to metric/trace events and generates weekly schema-drift digest.

Example CLI checks (ops quick commands):
- Validate manifest locally:
  $ redwood-manifest lint ./api-manifest.json

- Run lightweight schema-compat check against staging:
  $ redwood-manifest check-compat --manifest ./api-manifest.json --staging http://staging.synth.redwood.internal

Appendix: example small runbook snippet to attach to owner teams in their runbooks:
- If schema drift > 2%:
  1) Set sampling to 100% for 30 minutes.
  2) Collect 500 offending payloads to /tmp/schema-drift/ and open issue with link.
  3) If the drift is caused by an intentional extension, update manifest and canonical schema, run CI, and plan staggered rollout.

Related references and patterns:
- Use the existing telemetry taxonomy defined in observability-standards to name metrics.
- For model-backed responses, ensure model_version is emitted and matched to model artifact provenance docs.

Notes on scope creep and exceptions:
- Light internal-only endpoints can declare "internal_only": true in the manifest and opt-out of public SLO enforcement, but must still provide required observability keys.
- Teams may request temporary waivers for canary durations with SRE approval; such waivers are recorded on the deployment ticket.

Contact and ownership:
- Primary author: Aisha Patel (team-platform-infra)
- SRE contact: Marcus Chen (eng-sre)
- Validation tooling owner: Leah Martinez (eng-platform)

This document is normative: new public endpoints must include a manifest and pass the CI and canary validations as described. The SRE guild will audit manifests quarterly and publish a compliance report to the infra-standards space.
